title: KV epoch-pointer drift -> memory growth: investigation, immediate mitigations, and medium-term guardrails
creator: Asha Raman
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency customer workload on hosted inference (mixed short/long context requests), the KV cache began exhibiting sustained memory growth over several hours. The symptoms were increased OOMs on a subset of inference workers and degraded tail latency. This ticket captures the incident investigation, short-term mitigations applied during the event, root cause hypothesis (epoch-pointer drift leading to stale slab references and invisible fragments), and the consolidated action items to prevent recurrence.
steps_taken: 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC: Alert page triggered by RL agent - memory growth SLO breach for shard group eu-west-1a (dashboard: runtime-ops/mem-growth).
Immediate mitigation 03:20 UTC: Applied flow-control rule to throttle incoming prefix writes for affected customer route; triggered autoscaler to add warm nodes to the pool.
03:35 UTC: Rolled forward emergency hotfix v1.22.0-rc.3 to set GC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.6 and enable eviction-slowdown guard in runtime config (non-breaking runtime flag).
04:50 UTC: Performed rolling restart of affected worker group to reclaim slab memory from corrupted epoch references.
05:30 UTC: Observed memory curve flatten and tail latency recover to baseline; open follow-up required for root-cause fix and telemetry improvements.
timeline_notes: Detection window was ~3h from first anomaly to stable mitigation; but memory growth had begun ~22:00 local prior to alerts due to slow accumulation under bursty insertion pattern.
Operators initially suspected KV-key collision poisoning; telemetry showed low checksum-error rate but higher-than-normal allocation churn in slab allocator metrics (slab_alloc/compact/delta).
root_cause_summary: A race in the epoch-based pointer reclamation path allowed a pointer to a freed slab entry to be re-referenced after an epoch increment. Under specific interleaving of concurrent prefix inserts and asynchronous compaction, the runtime's eviction index could retain references to entries that had been logically freed but not physically zeroed. Over time these phantom references prevented slab pages from being reclaimed, causing fragmentation and unbounded memory growth. The failure mode is rare and manifests with specific concurrency and sequence length distributions (mixed short and long requests).
evidence: Heap histograms and slab page maps from affected instances (s3://redwood-incidents/kv-260501/heap-01.json).
Instrumented trace showing epoch bump with concurrent prefix insert and compact run (trace ID: 7a9f-epoch-2026-02-27).
Post-incident core dumps showing stale slab page refs (attached in incident bundle).
Replication run in staging reproduced leak using the workload generator (job: perf/kv/drift-repro-2026-03-02).
action_items: ENG-260502: Add deterministic eviction-index sweep that validates pointer epochs and logs mismatch events (owner: Linh Tran). Due 2026-03-10.
ENG-260503: Implement zeroing-on-free for slab pages in debug builds and enable in staging to catch use-after-free earlier (owner: Marco Diaz). Due 2026-03-17.
ENG-260504: Backport conservative GC policy that triggers compaction earlier when allocation churn spike > 20% (owner: Priya Nair). Due 2026-03-12.
ENG-260505: Add load generator scenario to CI that mimics the mixed short/long context burst pattern to catch regression early (owner: Diego Morales). Due 2026-03-24.
ENG-260506: Create a runtime guardrail feature flag to automatically throttle writes when slab fragmentation crosses threshold and add dashboard alert (owner: SRE team - Jason Lee). Due 2026-03-15.
ENG-260507: Add end-to-end test with chaos (concurrent compaction + inserts) to the nightly conformance suite (owner: QA - Maya Patel). Due 2026-03-31.
ENG-260508: Instrument eviction telemetry: per-index reference-count drift, compaction run durations, and epoch-mismatch counters (owner: Observability - Hitoshi Kato). Due 2026-03-10.
ENG-260509: Update runbook to include 'epoch-drift' diagnosis steps and a safe rollback playbook for rolling restarts (owner: Oncall - Diego Morales). Due 2026-03-05 (complete).
risk_and_tradeoffs: Zeroing-on-free increases CPU and write latency in debug builds; we will gate it to staging and selective builds before enabling in prod.
Lowering GC thresholds reduces memory headroom and may increase eviction churn under normal load; we'll couple change with autoscaler policy adjustments.
Aggressive write throttling protects memory but impacts customer throughput; we will expose guardrail as an opt-in runtime feature with telemetry-based auto-disable.
postmortem_decision_points: Do not immediately change slab allocator design in prod; instead implement telemetry and defensive patches to give time for a measured redesign.
Prioritize backport of compact-on-threshold and epoch-mismatch logging ahead of a full pointer-reclamation redesign.
Schedule a design review for a robust epoch-less reclamation approach in Q2 2026 (Architecture RFC).
followup_notes: Staging runs with zeroing-on-free exposed two unrelated logic errors in the compaction path; owners assigned and bugs filed (ENG-260610, ENG-260611).
Customer communication: Affected customers were notified with timeline and mitigation; dedicated follow-up calls scheduled for enterprise accounts impacted (account-rep: Priya Nair).
Telemetry patch (ENG-260508) landed and released to prod 2026-03-03; early warning alerts now prevent >30min undetected memory growth.
resolution_status: Mitigated in prod via roll-forward config + rolling restarts; short-term guardrails deployed. Medium-term fixes scoped and prioritized.
